az_doctor_s_office_the.blurb: A cool, shaded sport crag tucked into a narrow corridor between two rock fins in the Cave Springs part of Oak Creek Canyon, near Sedona. Eight routes, almost all bolted, with one trad line. Grades run from one easy 5.8 up through a handful of 5.11s, one 5.12 and a couple of 5.10s, so it suits climbers working at the harder end of moderate and above. One side is steep to slightly overhanging sandstone with pockets and edges, while the opposite side is a slabbier, darker rock. Because the canyon walls keep it out of the sun through the day, it makes a good pick when other crags are baking. Rock quality varies.
az_doctor_s_office_the.parking_note: Leave the car at the Cave Springs Campground area in Oak Creek Canyon, on the near side of the bridge over the creek.
az_doctor_s_office_the.approach: From the parking spot, cross the bridge and pick up the climbers' trail on the west bank of the creek. It heads up a small hillside, skirts around it and follows a wash into the corridor that holds the routes.

az_naiche_s_nest.blurb: A small, steep dome in the West Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, close to the Isle-of-you campground. Roughly 50 feet tall, it holds eight short routes: six sport or top-rope lines and two trad lines. Most grades sit in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, with one 5.10 and one 5.11, which makes it a handy spot for newer leaders and for anyone wanting a quick top-rope lap. The wall is a touch past vertical. It sees little traffic compared with the campground beside it. Shade arrives in the morning and sun hits not long after noon, so pick your season and time of day accordingly.

az_not_so_steep.blurb: A small crag high on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains, in the Upper Highway zone. It faces east and is open and sunny. Eight short routes, mostly bolted with five or six bolts and chain anchors, plus one line that is protected with gear. Grades span the easier 5.7s up to 5.10, with most routes at 5.9 or below, so it is a comfortable place for newer leaders. The crag sits just a few minutes on foot from its steeper neighbour, across a low-angle slab, which makes it an easy add-on to a bigger day up the mountain.

az_tombstone_the_2.blurb: A standalone, prism-shaped formation in the West Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, marked out by lichen-covered faces and a large offwidth on its western side. Everything here is trad, with eight single-pitch lines. Five fall in the 5.10 range, then there is one each at 5.11, 5.12 and 5.13, so it leans toward experienced climbers who like cracks and want a compact, no-nonsense day. The walk in is a casual hike across open ground, with some brush possible. Descent is by rappel. It is not a good choice for dogs, and the hike makes it a place for a focused objective rather than a casual stop.

az_vista_boulder.blurb: A lone boulder on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains, reached from the San Pedro Vista Overlook. It stands about 8 feet tall and leans out at roughly 45 degrees over a flat landing. Eight problems are packed onto it, from an easy V0 through a few V2 and V3 lines to a V4 and a pair of hard problems at V8 and V9, so there is something for most levels but a lot of the interest is at the top end. It sees little traffic and works well for a short solo session or an add-on stop while driving the highway.
az_vista_boulder.parking_note: Park at the San Pedro Vista Overlook lot, off the Mount Lemmon highway near mile 17.6, which doubles as the parking for this boulder.
